title: Does DETECTOR-produced perception (HUD + mover, from real arcade frames) recover gemma-4-31B's goal induction, matching the hand-authored oracle's 7/8?
methodology_note: Same model + same learned RULES per game as REQ-ARC-WMTE-5832; the ONLY change is the perception SOURCE -- hand-authored oracle facts (5832) replaced by perceive_entities() output run on real offline-arcade transitions (5833 detectors). Compares detector perception to the oracle's 7/8. Detectors + arcade use no LLM. Public-game frames stepped for offline dev validation (authorized), never in the hidden submission.
baseline_oracle_result: REQ-ARC-WMTE-5832 hand-authored oracle: 7/8 correct + 1 partial, 0 wrong (naive was 0/8).

headline: HONEST NEGATIVE: detector-produced perception did NOT recover the hand-authored oracle's 7/8. Result: 0 correct, 2 partial (ls20, cn04 -- the games where a mover was detected, both produced the RIGHT SHAPE 'move the player to a target'), 6 wrong. Root causes: (1) the model's OWN WRONG learned RULES (e.g. bp35 'action 6 changes (63,x) to 15', lf52 'actions change row 0') DOMINATE -- the detector's 'ignore this counter band' note is weaker than a rule the model already believes; (2) the detector NAMES the player but cannot NAME which object is the exit/target, so even mover-games stay vague; (3) the mover was missed on 4/8 games (tu93/bp35/lf52/r11l), leaving no player concept. The oracle worked because it REPLACED the framing (explicitly 'the bar is a lose-timer, NOT the objective' + named the exit); the detector ADDS entities alongside the wrong rules instead of correcting them.
next_step: The perception fix must RE-AUTHOR, not augment: (a) RETRACT any learned rule that references a detected HUD band ('your note that action 6 changes row 63 describes a status counter -- discard it as the goal'); (b) propose the mover's nearest distinct object as the candidate TARGET so 'move the player to X' is concrete; (c) improve mover recall on the 4 missed games. This converts 'adds entities beside wrong rules' into 'corrects the wrong framing' -- what the oracle did to get 7/8.
